| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

Question 1
?
x 1 2 3 4 5
y 3 −2 −1 1 −1

The vector of coefficients of the curve y=β0+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

[β0β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[1123122−2132−11421152−1]
b
[131−21−1111−1]
c
[112122132142152]
d
[11121222133214421552]
e
[1112131415]
Submit

decision.explanation: Each row of X contains the coefficients multiplying β₀ and β₂: [1, x²]. Thus the design matrix has columns 1 and x², giving option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & {1}^{2} \\ 1 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & {5}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

[β0β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a

[131−21−1111−1]

[112122132142152]

[11121222133214421552]

EXPLANATION
x 1 2 3 4 5
y 3 −2 −1 1 −1

The coefficients of the curve

y=β0+β2x2

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

[112122132142152]⏞X[β0β2]⏞β=[3−2−11−1]⏞y,

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Design Matrix When the Regression Curve Contains Zero Coefficients
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & {1}^{2} \\ 1 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & {5}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

decision.explanation: The model has terms β₀, β₁x, β₂x², and β₃x³, so each design-matrix row is [1, x, x², x³]. For x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, this is option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $5$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $5$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & {0}^{2} & {0}^{3} \\ 1 & 1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -1 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Elements of a Polynomial Regression Model
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $5$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $5$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & {0}^{2} & {0}^{3} \\ 1 & 1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -1 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

decision.explanation: The observation vector contains the measured y-values in table order: −1, −5, −3, −4, 5. This is option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-1$ | $-5$ | $-3$ | $-4$ | $5$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-1$ | $-5$ | $-3$ | $-4$ | $5$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2} & {5}^{3} \\ 1 & 7 & {7}^{2} & {7}^{3} \\ 1 & 9 & {9}^{2} & {9}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -5 \\ -3 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

x 1 3 5 7 9

[β0β1β2β3]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[13579]
b
[−1−5−3−45]
c
[11121332155217721992]
d
[111213133233155253177273199293]
e
[1−1(−1)2(−1)31−5(−5)2(−5)31−3(−3)2(−3)31−4(−4)2(−4)3155253]

[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-1$ | $-5$ | $-3$ | $-4$ | $5$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2} & {5}^{3} \\ 1 & 7 & {7}^{2} & {7}^{3} \\ 1 & 9 & {9}^{2} & {9}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -5 \\ -3 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

?
x −1 0 1 2 3
y 2 9 0 −9 −12

The vector of coefficients of the curve y=β0+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

[β0β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[1−1(−1)21002111212221332]
b
[−1209102−93−12]
c
[1−110111213]
d
[−1(−1)2002112222332]
e
[1(−1)2102112122132]
Submit

decision.explanation: The model y = β₀ + β₂x² requires each row of X to be [1, x²]. Substituting x = −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 gives option e.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $2$ | $9$ | $0$ | $-9$ | $-12$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $2$ | $9$ | $0$ | $-9$ | $-12$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & (-1)^{2} \\ 1 & {0}^{2} \\ 1 & {1}^{2} \\ 1 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & {3}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 9 \\ 0 \\ -9 \\ -12\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Design Matrix When the Regression Curve Contains Zero Coefficients
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $2$ | $9$ | $0$ | $-9$ | $-12$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $2$ | $9$ | $0$ | $-9$ | $-12$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & (-1)^{2} \\ 1 & {0}^{2} \\ 1 & {1}^{2} \\ 1 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & {3}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 9 \\ 0 \\ -9 \\ -12\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.
